- **Target files:** Claude Code's MCP settings go to `.mcp.json`, and OpenAI Codex CLI's go to `.codex/config.toml`. Gemini CLI uses `.gemini/settings.json`. Several open-source tools do this, and most treat one config as the source of truth.

- **sync-agents-settings** makes Claude Code the single source for MCP settings and syncs to Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, and several others. It also handles instruction files, and it covers the Codex project-level config. **Claude Code is the single source of truth** for MCP settings, synced to all supported targets.
- **mcp-sync (ejfn)** uses your `~/.claude.json` as the input and writes to Gemini CLI and Codex. It has a `--prune` option that removes servers from targets when they're gone from the source. It also notes that Codex accepts only stdio servers. OpenAI Codex CLI (~/.codex/config.toml) - Uses mcp_servers key in TOML format (Codex only supports servers of type stdio)
- **mcpport (Abdalkaderdev)** lists, lints, syncs, and converts configs across Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. It is read-only for Claude Code local-scope servers. Claude Code local-scope servers are read as a source, never written to.
- **mcp-sync (EnjoyableWork)** uses its own canonical file at `~/.config/mcp-sync/config.json`, not a client config, and writes to Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, and Codex. mcp-sync establishes a single local source of truth at ~/.config/mcp-sync/config.json.
- **mcp-sync (docs.rs)** reads one `mcp.yaml` file and targets Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode. It includes a watch mode.
- **holstein13/mcp-config-manager** is an interactive tool that toggles servers and syncs between Claude, Gemini, and Codex, with timestamped backups. Its sync is between Claude and Gemini/Codex rather than from one canonical file.

Config locations are consistent across tools. Claude Code uses `~/.claude.json`, Gemini CLI uses `~/.gemini/settings.json` (JSON, `mcpServers` key), and Codex CLI uses `~/.codex/config.toml` (TOML, `mcp_servers` key). The main difference is the format, since Codex uses TOML and the others use JSON.

I didn't check the install status, maintenance activity, or licenses of these projects, so verify those before relying on one.

content.content:
**Supported targets:** Antigravity (VS Code extension), Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and custom targets loaded as dynamic libraries. Gemini CLI is not listed.

**Canonical file:** `mcp.yaml` by default, set with `--canon <PATH or URL>`. It can also be loaded from a remote URL.

**Install:** `cargo install --path .` from a local checkout. The page shows no crates.io install command.

**First run:**
- `mcp-sync sync` performs a one-time sync to all targets.
- `mcp-sync sync --dry-run --verbose` previews changes without writing files.
- `mcp-sync init --output mcp.yaml` runs an interactive wizard to create the canonical file.
- `mcp-sync validate --canon mcp.yaml` checks the file.

**Preserving other settings:** The page doesn't say whether unrelated settings in target files are kept. It does say that before modifying a file, mcp-sync creates a timestamped backup, such as `config.json.bak.20260105-230041`.

**Global vs. project scope:** `--scope` accepts `global`, `project`, or `both`, and defaults to `both`. Global files are user-level, such as `~/.claude.json` for Claude and `~/.codex/config.toml` for Codex. Project files are `.mcp.json` for Claude, `.vscode/mcp.json` for Antigravity, `.codex/config.toml` for Codex, and `opencode.json` for OpenCode. The project root defaults to auto-detected git root, and `--project-root` overrides it.

**Prune behavior:** The `--clean` flag removes servers that aren't in the canonical file. The page doesn't say whether this applies to every target or how it interacts with backups.

**License:** MIT.

content.content:
**Repo:** Abdalkaderdev/mcpport, a CLI that lists, lints, syncs, and converts MCP server configs.

- **Canonical source file:** None is named. Each agent is a row in `src/config.ts` that parses its config into a shared internal shape. The README's translation table uses Claude Code's format as its reference column, but that is not a separate file.
- **Supported targets:** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Cursor. VS Code, Windsurf, Zed, and Claude Desktop are on the roadmap.
- **Install:** `npx mcpport <command>` or `npm i -g mcpport`. Requires Node 22+.
- **First run:** `npx mcpport list`, then `npx mcpport lint`, then `npx mcpport sync claude cursor` to preview a sync.
- **Preserves other settings:** Yes. JSON files keep unrelated keys, and Codex TOML keeps comments and unrelated tables. The README says Claude Code's `~/.claude.json` is rewritten with 2-space indentation, which is how Claude Code writes it.
- **Backups:** Yes. The target file is copied to `<file>.<timestamp>.bak` before each write, and writes go through a temp file and rename.
- **Dry run:** `sync` is a dry run unless `--apply` is passed. `list`, `lint`, and `convert` without `--apply` or `--out` are read-only.
- **License:** MIT.
- **Activity and popularity:** 14 commits, 0 stars, 0 forks, and 0 watchers. The page doesn't show a last-commit date, so recent activity can't be confirmed from it.

content.content:
**sync-agents-settings** (MIT license) copies MCP server configs and instruction files from Claude Code to other AI coding agents.

- **Source of truth:** Claude Code. The tool reads `~/.claude.json` and enabled plugin `.mcp.json` files. The README states that "Claude Code is the single source of truth" for MCP settings.
- **Supported targets:** Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Kiro CLI, Cursor, Kimi CLI, Vibe CLI, Qwen Code, Amp, Cline CLI, and Windsurf. Instruction sync also covers Aider.
- **Install commands:**
  - Claude Code plugin: `claude plugin marketplace add Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings`, then `claude plugin install sync-agents-settings`
  - No install: `npx sync-agents-settings list`
  - Global: `npm install -g sync-agents-settings`, then run `sync-agents`
- **First-run commands:** The page has no section labeled first run. Its examples suggest this order: `list`, then `sync --dry-run`, then `sync`.
- **Dry-run:** `--dry-run` previews changes without writing files.
- **Backups:** Before writing, each sync copies affected config files to `~/.sync-agents-backup/<timestamp>/`, keeping their paths relative to `~`. `--no-backup` skips this. Missing target directories are skipped, not created.
- **Preserves other settings:** Existing settings stay intact (for example, a Gemini theme or an OpenCode model). Existing servers are never overwritten, so re-running is safe.
- **Stars and activity:** 7 stars, 1 fork, 1 watcher, and 37 commits on `main`. The page doesn't show a date for the last activity.

input.prompt: Does ruler support global/user-level MCP config (writing to ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.gemini/settings.json) or only project-level? Install command, init/apply commands, merge behavior with existing settings, backups, dry-run, license, stars.

toolu_01NQkgtP6F5KYsHc7NuUK42D.prompt: Does ruler support global/user-level MCP config (writing to ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.gemini/settings.json) or only project-level? Install command, init/apply commands, merge behavior with existing settings, backups, dry-run, license, stars.

content.content:
**Short answer: project-level only.** The README states that "Ruler never writes MCP configuration files outside your project root." It targets only project-local paths, so it won't write to `~/.claude.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, or `~/.gemini/settings.json`. For Codex, you point `CODEX_HOME` at the project's `.codex` directory. The only global location is Ruler's own config directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ruler`), used for rules when no local `.ruler/` exists.

- **Install:** Run `npm install -g @intellectronica/ruler`, or use `npx @intellectronica/ruler`. Node `^20.19.0 || ^22.12.0 || >=23` is required.
- **Init:** `ruler init` creates `.ruler/`, `.ruler/AGENTS.md`, and `.ruler/ruler.toml`. `ruler init --global` creates the global config.
- **Apply:** `ruler apply` writes agent config files. Use `--agents` to target specific agents.
- **Merge:** The default strategy is merge. `--mcp-overwrite` replaces native MCP config instead. TOML servers take precedence over legacy JSON servers with the same name.
- **Backups:** Ruler creates `.bak` copies of existing non-Ruler-generated config files before replacing them. This is on by default and controlled with `--backup`/`--no-backup`.
- **Dry-run:** `ruler apply --dry-run` previews changes without writing files.
- **License:** MIT.
- **Stars:** About 3.0k, with 165 forks.

toolu_01RCZ9YQSJraycMSRwtS9i8r.prompt: Supported targets (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI?), is there a single master server list, install, first-run commands, backups, preserves other settings, license, stars, requires GUI?

content.content:
**Supported targets:** Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Codex, and Kiro. The page doesn't mention Claude Code or Gemini CLI. Codex CLI is covered: the Codex target manages the global host config shared by the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI, and the Codex IDE extension.

**Install:**
- Homebrew: `brew install EnjoyableWork/tap/mcp-sync`
- Windows: `winget install EnjoyableWork.mcp-sync`
- Cargo: `cargo install enjoyable-mcp-sync` (the crate name differs, but it installs the `mcp-sync` executable)
- GitHub Releases: prebuilt archives for macOS, Linux, and Windows

**First-run commands:**
1. `mcp-sync init` creates the canonical config from discovered client files. It won't overwrite an existing file.
2. Optionally, `mcp-sync add <name> --command <cmd> --arg ... --env KEY=VALUE` adds a server.
3. `mcp-sync list` shows server names and env key names without values.
4. `mcp-sync test <name>` starts the configured process for a bounded MCP handshake. Only this command runs servers.
5. `mcp-sync sync --dry-run` previews the changes, then `mcp-sync sync` applies them.

**Dry run:** `sync --dry-run` validates everything and prints the redacted plan for all six targets without writing anything.

**Backups:** Each changed managed file gets one adjacent `.bak` copy, replaced on the next change. There's no time-based expiration, and new files have no backup. To keep longer history, copy the files elsewhere. `mcp-sync restore <target>` restores a file, and `--dry-run` previews it first.

**Preserving other settings:** Client-only fields, unrelated settings, comments (for Kiro), target-only servers, and unmanaged remote entries survive a sync. There's no implicit pruning. Entries mcp-sync can't represent are left unmanaged rather than rewritten.

**License:** MIT.

**Stars:** The repo shows 0 stars, 0 watchers, and 0 forks.

content.content:
- **Supported targets:** Claude (`~/.claude.json`), Gemini (`~/.gemini/settings.json`), and Codex (`~/.codex.json`). The README says it manages "`.claude.json`, `.gemini/settings.json`, and Codex configuration files." Claude Code, Gemini CLI, and Codex are listed as prerequisites.

- **Single master server list:** The page doesn't describe one. Its closest equivalent is an "All (synced)" mode that keeps the three configs synchronized. Disabled servers are stored separately in `~/.mcp_disabled_servers.json`.

- **Install:** Use the one-line `install.sh` installer (curl piped to bash), which sets up an isolated Python environment and adds an `mcp` command to your PATH. For manual installation, clone the repo and run `pip install -e .` (Python 3.8+). PyQt6 is optional.

- **First-run commands:** After the quick install, run `mcp gui` (recommended), `mcp interactive`, or `mcp status`. The manual install uses `mcp-config-manager` instead of `mcp`.

- **Backups:** Timestamped backups are created automatically before changes, and you can run a manual backup. Backups go to `~/Documents/MCP Config Manager/backups/`, with legacy backups in `~/.claude.json.backup.*`. You can restore from the GUI or with the `restore` command.

- **Preserves other settings:** Not explicitly stated. The page only says enable/disable doesn't lose configurations and that the tool uses the same file locations as the original script.

- **License:** MIT.

- **Stars:** 29 stars, 7 forks, 1 watcher, and 1 open issue.

- **Requires GUI?** No. The CLI interactive mode and command-line commands work without it. The GUI uses PyQt6 if installed and falls back to tkinter otherwise.

input.prompt: Exact CLI usage: how to target only gemini and codex (flag name and values), how updates to existing servers or removed servers are handled (overwrite/prune options?), how http/sse servers are converted for Codex, whether project-level scope is supported, Node version required, and any 'diff' or 'list' commands. Quote command examples verbatim.

toolu_0147jhKTv3XmvhY8K9PkAssX.prompt: Exact CLI usage: how to target only gemini and codex (flag name and values), how updates to existing servers or removed servers are handled (overwrite/prune options?), how http/sse servers are converted for Codex, whether project-level scope is supported, Node version required, and any 'diff' or 'list' commands. Quote command examples verbatim.

content.content:
**Targeting gemini and codex**

Single-target sync examples use one `--target` value per command:

```
sync-agents sync --target gemini
sync-agents sync --target codex
```

The README shows multiple values (space-separated) for `doctor`, `reconcile`, and `diff`:

```
sync-agents doctor --target gemini codex
sync-agents reconcile --target gemini codex
sync-agents diff --report json --target gemini codex
```

It does not show multiple values for `sync` itself.

**Updates, removals, and overwrite/prune**

- Existing servers are never overwritten, and re-running sync does not overwrite existing entries.
- No prune or removal option for MCP sync is documented, and the README doesn't say what happens to servers deleted from Claude Code.
- `--on-conflict overwrite|append|skip` is documented only for instruction-file sync (`sync-instructions`), not MCP sync.
- Backups are created by default before writing. `--no-backup` skips them.

**HTTP/SSE conversion for Codex**

Both `http` and `sse` servers are written with a `url` field, and no `type` field is needed. Codex doesn't support `${VAR:-default}` syntax, so those values are expanded during sync to the environment value or the default.

**Project-level scope**

Yes, for several targets. Codex uses `--codex-home`, for example:

```
sync-agents sync --target codex --codex-home ./my-project/.codex
```

Kimi, Vibe, Qwen, Amp, Cline, and Windsurf have similar `--<tool>-home` flags. Gemini has no documented project-level flag. Codex does not merge global and project configs. When a project has `.codex/`, the global `~/.codex/` directory is ignored.

**Node version**

The README doesn't state it in prose. The Node.js badge indicates `>=18`.

**diff and list commands**

```
sync-agents diff
sync-agents diff --report json --target gemini codex
npx sync-agents-settings list
sync-agents list
```

`diff` compares configs between Claude and other agents. `list` shows MCP servers detected from Claude Code. `doctor` checks for drift and parse errors.

content.text:
I couldn't find a single well-established tool that does exactly this. The closest fit is **sync-agents-settings**. It treats Claude Code's own config as your one list and copies those servers into Gemini CLI and Codex CLI, leaving their other settings alone. I've only read the READMEs and haven't run any of these tools. All of them are small projects with few stars, so skim the code before you let one write to your configs.

**My assumptions:** you want your user-wide configs synced (`~/.claude.json`, `~/.gemini/settings.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`) rather than per-project files, and you have Node.js installed.

## Main recommendation: sync-agents-settings

[Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings](https://github.com/Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings), MIT license, runs locally, no account.

**Why it fits:**
- You keep adding servers the usual way (`claude mcp add …`), and Claude Code's config becomes the master list.
- It writes Gemini's JSON and Codex's TOML for you. HTTP/SSE servers are converted to a `url` entry for Codex.
- The README says existing settings stay intact (for example, a Gemini theme). It also backs up each file to `~/.sync-agents-backup/<timestamp>/` before writing.
- It has `--dry-run`, `diff` and `doctor` (checks for drift and parse errors), and it skips any agent that isn't installed.

**Limitations:**
- **It only adds servers.** It never overwrites a server that already exists in a target, and the README doesn't document any way to remove servers. If you change or delete a server in Claude Code, you'll still need to fix it by hand in the other two, or try its `reconcile` command, whose exact behaviour I couldn't confirm.
- The README only shows one `--target` per `sync` command.

**Install (needs Node 18+):**
```bash
npm install -g sync-agents-settings
# or run it without installing: npx sync-agents-settings <command>
```

**First run:**
```bash
sync-agents list                         # servers it found in Claude Code
sync-agents diff --target gemini codex   # how the others differ
sync-agents sync --target gemini --dry-run
sync-agents sync --target codex --dry-run
sync-agents sync --target gemini         # write for real (backs up first)
sync-agents sync --target codex
sync-agents doctor --target gemini codex # check for drift or parse errors
```
After that, each time you add a server: `claude mcp add …`, then run the two `sync` commands again.

## Alternatives

| Tool | Why you might pick it | Drawback |
|---|---|---|
| [mcpport](https://github.com/Abdalkaderdev/mcpport) (`npm i -g mcpport`, Node 22+) | Covers Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor. `sync` only previews unless you add `--apply`. Keeps unrelated keys, and keeps comments in Codex's TOML. Makes timestamped backups. | No separate master file: you sync from one agent to another, e.g. `mcpport sync claude gemini --apply`. 0 stars. |
| [EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync](https://github.com/EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync) (`brew install EnjoyableWork/tap/mcp-sync`) | Has its own master file (`~/.config/mcp-sync/config.json`), keeps other settings, never deletes servers on its own. | Its documented targets are Codex, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code and Kiro. **It doesn't list Claude Code or Gemini CLI.** |
| [mcp-config-manager](https://github.com/holstein13/mcp-config-manager) (Python) | Built for Claude, Gemini and Codex, with enable/disable and backups. | The Codex path in its README is `~/.codex.json`, not `config.toml`, which suggests it's out of date for current Codex. Its installer is `curl \| bash`. It doesn't say whether it keeps other settings. |
| [mcp-sync (Rust)](https://docs.rs/crate/mcp-sync/latest/source/README.md) | Master `mcp.yaml`, `--dry-run`, `--clean` to remove servers that aren't in the master file. | Doesn't support Gemini CLI. |
| [Ruler](https://github.com/intellectronica/ruler) (~3k stars) | The most established tool here. Its `ruler.toml` keeps one MCP list for Claude, Codex and Gemini. | **Per-project only.** It never writes MCP config outside the project folder, so it doesn't fit if you want user-wide settings. |

**Bottom line:** use sync-agents-settings if you're happy for Claude Code to hold the master list. Try mcpport if you'd rather see a preview before every write and want Codex's TOML comments kept. Use Ruler only if you manage MCP servers per project. Whichever you choose, back up the three config files yourself before the first real sync.

Sources:
- [sync-agents-settings](https://github.com/Leoyang183/sync-agents-settings)
- [mcpport](https://github.com/Abdalkaderdev/mcpport)
- [EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync](https://github.com/EnjoyableWork/mcp-sync)
- [holstein13/mcp-config-manager](https://github.com/holstein13/mcp-config-manager)
- [mcp-sync (docs.rs)](https://docs.rs/crate/mcp-sync/latest/source/README.md)
- [intellectronica/ruler](https://github.com/intellectronica/ruler)
- [ejfn/mcp-sync](https://github.com/ejfn/mcp-sync) (appeared in search, but the repo returned 404)
